To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electrogenic Solute Linked Carrier 26 (SLC26) transporters can function as both uncoupled channels and coupled transporters, and the conserved Glutamic acid residue is essential for their transport function.
the conserved Glutamate residue (E357) is critical for coupled transport and uncouple channel‐like activity by SLC26a6.
The electrogenic SLC 26 transporters mediate coupled transport and uncouple to form channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the function of the SLC transporters.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms that underlie the transport of diverse substrates by the SLC26 anion exchangers and channels.
the molecular mechanism underlying the function of electrogenic SLC transporters, which mediate the transport and exchange of diverse molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E357A mutation of Slc26A6 eliminates all forms of coupled anion transport, but increases the channel‐like current.

the Glu‐ residue in Slc26A3 and Slc6A6 is a key residue that determines the transport modes of these proteins, with the charge of the residue playing an important role in determining the transport mode.

the Glu‐ residue in SLC26 transport proteins is essential for the coupled transport mode and that its charge is critical for the uncoupled transport mode, and that the charge of this residue is critical for determining the stoichiometry and kinetics of coupled transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a conserved Glu residue is required for coupled transport by Slc26a, but is not essential for channel‐like activity.

the E357 in Slc26A6 and E367 in Slc26 A3 are important determinants of the coupled transport mode of the SLC 26 transporters and that the conserved Glus in Slc26s are critical for the coupled transport mode and may play a role in determining the stoichiometry.
the Glu‐ in the predicted transmembrane domain 10 of Slc26 family members determines the coupled transport activity, and the charge of Glu‐ determines the coupled transport direction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a conserved Glu residue in the SLC26 transport family plays a critical role in determining the coupled and uncoupling modes of transport by these proteins.
the same structural motif in Slc26s can determine both the coupled transport and uncoulpled channel‐like activities.
the conserved E‐ (in Slc26a4, Slc26A6, and Slc26A3) is important for the coupled transport mode and the neutralization of this E‐ abolishes the coupled transport and augments the uncoupled transport.
